items.reason: Pinning a tag needs GitHub's API to say what the tag points at, and this session has no network; the repo already ships the one-command close (`npm run actions:pin`, which also flips STRICT and raises the ratchet in the same pass), so there is nothing to add offline but a fabricated SHA.

`npm run agents:surface` now reads the generated regions instead of only hashing them: an instruction-shaped line that is not in the accepted lock content fails the gate, and `--accept` refuses to pin a newly arrived one without `--accept-instructions`.

A surviving-mutant ceiling is a measurement, and this session has no test runner, no package manager and no network; note that the gate scripts already have a known-bad-fixture suite (test-unit/gate-bite.test.mjs) and the chokepoint has fault injection (test-unit/fault-injection-llm.test.mjs), so the honest remaining gap is mutation evidence over the store seams.

The ordering has to be derived from red-build history, and none exists offline — `.gate-timings.json` is git-ignored and absent in a fresh worktree and there is no committed `.github/gate-timings.json`; added `npm run gates:failures`, which reads the `failedAt` the timed runs already record, so the maintainer can produce the ranking in one run.

lessons: In this repository a new check must be blocking-by-construction or ratcheted — never blocking-on-a-guess. With no way to run the gate, the safe shape is to derive the baseline from an artefact already committed (here: the accepted lock content), so the rule is provably green on today's tree whatever the classifier's exact matching turns out to be.

Adding an ADR here has a side effect worth planning for: `scripts/adr-check.mjs` settles a record once three higher-numbered ones exist, so ADR-0012 made ADR-0009's `## Consequences observed` section due in the same commit.
